current.text: Brooklyn added Julius Randle, who is projected to start at power forward.
The Randle trade kills Wolf's value at power forward.
Wolf is projected as a bench player. The bench rotation is Keon Ellis, Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Wolf and Nolan Traore, and Day'Ron Sharpe is the projected starting center.

Brooklyn's center minutes will likely be a messy split between Sharpe, Wagner and Wolf. One expert saw a path for Wolf to start at center over Sharpe. Check early in the season whether Sharpe really starts.
Experts see no clear breakout for him.

Brooklyn is projected near the bottom of the league, at about 28 wins. Houston owns the Nets' pick, so March minutes are uncertain: the team has no reason to tank, but little reason to win beyond player development.
With a March 28 end, Brooklyn plays 3-4-3 games in our playoff weeks, with only one playoff back-to-back. The Nets have 16 back-to-backs this season, tied for the most in the league.

durable.text: He can play center and can also handle the ball.
He is a poor efficiency player across the board and a weak defender.
Experts rate him a poor NBA player. One calls him legitimately terrible, and another doubts he is an NBA player at all.

note: Wolf is not a draft target. Both sites value him at 0 USD (ESPN average cost 0.1 USD), Yahoo ranks him 332, and nobody took him in our league last season. No category stands out, so he fits no punt build, and his 40.5% FG on 7.7 attempts last season matches the expert view that he is inefficient. Early in the season, watch on waivers whether Sharpe actually holds the starting center job. Wolf only becomes worth a look if he wins real center minutes.
